The main takeaway from our work is that
the crystallization history of this sample is complex and not well represented by a simple model of equilibrium crystallization at a single, constant cooling rate.
the crystallization of a basaltic composition can produce a variety of textures and mineralogies at cooling rates that are within the range of those inferred for lunar volcanism.
the crystallization of lunar picrites is sensitive to cooling rate, and this sensitivity is a function of the composition.
